einzeiler: The baffling 1948 case of an unidentified man found dead on Somerton Beach.
kurzfassung: On November 30, 1948, a well-dressed man was found dead on Somerton Beach in South Australia with no identification and all clothing tags removed. Decades later, DNA analysis identified him as Carl Charles Webb, an electrical engineer from Melbourne. Despite knowing his identity, key questions remain regarding his cause of death, a cryptic code, and his connection to a local nurse.
stichpunkte: A well-dressed man was found slumped against a sea wall on Somerton Beach on November 30, 1948.
Every clothing label and laundry mark had been systematically cut out from the man's garments.
Police later found an unclaimed suitcase at the Adelaide railway station containing tools, a tailored knife, and clothing with similar cut-out tags.
A hidden fob pocket in the man's trousers contained a torn slip of paper reading 'Tamam Shud' from a copy of the Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam.
A local copy of the Rubaiyat was later recovered containing an uncrackable code and the phone number of a nearby nurse.
An autopsy revealed severe internal congestion and damage, suggesting a rare poison, though toxicology screens were blank.
A late witness report from 1959 described seeing a man carrying another body across the beach on the night in question.
In 2022, DNA extracted from a preserved death mask identified the unknown man as electrical engineer Carl Charles Webb.
beschreibung:
On November 30, 1948 in South Australia, a man in a suit appeared on the beach.
Despite the many efforts of detectives, scientists, and the public, the man could not be identified. What made this mystery bizarre, was that there were cryptic messages and clues that made no sense. A small rolled up piece of paper, no labels on his clothing, and no apparent signs of struggle. However, in 2022, science finally caught up with the case and the identity was revealed. But even with that information, the case still remains a mystery.
